prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Marlinstone forecasts intents/performance-history. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module recalculates Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector constraints on configuration/weather/staffing/workload changes. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;Pushback Window Token at freeze. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Halcyon publication-confirms/checks recovered-plan slot-compliance;Saffron confirms pre-freeze;Aircraft Operator Representative reviews timing/stand feasibility(maintenance/fueling/boarding/cabin);changes justified. Foxglove read-only except coordination-roles;shows departure-fix pressure;stands cannot override accepted airspace constraints. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones(≤5s/validated-event);Adapter verifies reopened-apron clearance,sensors support;Adapter→Skylark/Ironleaf:occupancy/equipment-status. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities. Brindle advised only for runway-sequence/taxi-duration/metering

New part:
S490: The Data Governance Steward ensures that passenger connection information used for prioritization is aggregated or role-restricted so that operational users see only the detail required for recovery decisions.
S491: Diversion and irregular operations handling extends the operational concept beyond planned flow control by supporting safe acceptance, prioritization, communication, and recovery during the Recovery Phase and the Contingency Fallback State.
S492: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Regional Flow Platform to maintain a ranked view of candidate diversions, expected arrival times, required services, and the operational consequence of accepting each aircraft.
S493: The Demand Prediction Service compares amended Flight Intent Message data with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate to show whether a diversion can be absorbed without creating unsafe demand peaks.
S494: The Capacity Assessment Module evaluates runway availability, stand availability, sector load, handling capacity, and service constraints before a diversion recommendation is displayed.
S495: The Arrival Regulation Console presents diversion options with estimated holding exposure, likely gate or stand impact, and any expected effect on regulated arrivals already in the plan.
S496: The Airport Duty Manager sends the Medical Diversion Notice when a medical priority aircraft requires airport-level coordination before landing.
S497: Medical priority cases are treated as time-critical movements, and the operational objective is to minimize airborne delay while ensuring that emergency reception, surface routing, and stand access are ready.
S498: Technical priority cases include aircraft with abnormal system indications, degraded performance, fuel limitations, or maintenance requirements that make continued flight or extended holding undesirable.
S499: The Emergency Response Coordinator confirms rescue, medical, and airport safety readiness with the Airport Duty Manager before the arrival sequence is adjusted for a priority case.
S500: The Tower Supervisor coordinates airborne sequencing with the Airspace Sector Planner so that priority handling does not overload approach sectors or create unstable runway demand.
S501: The Airspace Sector Planner protects sector margins and may request a Tactical Regulation Proposal when diversion traffic requires a broader arrival management action.
S502: The Slot Coordinator reviews the effect of diversion acceptance on Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time commitments for departures that are already in a Slot Compliance State.
S503: The Airport CDM Portal uses the window token to preserve the agreed pushback opportunity when diversion recovery requires a protected departure movement.
S504: Communication sequencing follows the principle that safety status is confirmed first, airspace and runway feasibility second, airport resource readiness third, and passenger or network recovery actions last.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
